basis: Alopecia and metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with cone-shaped epiphyses define trichoscyphodysplasia.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, not an isolated hair disorder ([clinical report](https://doi.org/10.1002/ajmg.a.20411)).

basis: Junctional skin blistering, intellectual disability and characteristic dental defects define this syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental enamel defects are part of the syndrome definition ([MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/341663)); the supplied synonym also describes anodontia.

basis: Cryptophthalmos, urinary tract agenesis and syndactyly are major Fraser features, each reported in ~75%; individual intestinal and airway defects occur in 25%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: cutaneous syndactyly is a congenital digital fusion assigned to musculoskeletal; it does not establish an additional independent skin disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: syndactyly is a major diagnostic feature of Fraser syndrome and occurs in 3/4 patients, including its cutaneous form.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus 9/18 and cardiac dysrhythmias 8/18 support involvement ([original cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10932913/)).

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus affects 9/18 (~50%) in the original cohort; esotropia 4/18 is a subset and should not replace the overall strabismus frequency.

basis: Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration; postaxial polydactyly in 2/6 (~33%) does not establish functionally damaging skeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly reaches ~33% in a small cohort, but no associated skeletal dysfunction or destructive lesion is documented; frequency alone is insufficient.

basis: Developmental and skeletal abnormalities define KAT6B disorders; heart defects >50% ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK114806/)); ocular involvement ~50-60%.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis 11/18 (61%) and blepharophimosis 8/16 (50%) support common eyelid involvement ([cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8580094/)).

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; hepatic steatosis/injury and muscle-fiber pathology each occur in 1/2. Respiratory distress alone does not demonstrate intrinsic pulmonary damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: hypotonia/head lag in 1/2 do not establish brain or nerve damage; elevated brain/CSF lactate alone is metabolic evidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: muscle-fiber abnormalities in 1/2 support direct mitochondrial myopathy ([original report](https://doi.org/10.1093/hmg/ddt295)).

basis: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma defines hematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes; functionally damaging hepatic involvement at >=30% is not established for this subtype.

decisions.hepatic: none: generic ALL hepatomegaly/infiltration estimates do not establish functionally damaging liver involvement in >=30% of PAX5 P80R cases.

basis: Autoimmune skeletal-muscle necrosis; dysphagia (30-79%) reflects swallowing-muscle dysfunction, without established separate GI damage. Lung and cardiac lesions are <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent dysphagia (30-79%) is attributable to affected skeletal swallowing muscles; it does not establish direct gastrointestinal tissue disease.

basis: Altitude-induced central respiratory-control dysfunction defines recurrent sleep apnea; cardiovascular harm is a later risk, not established common direct damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: dysfunctional brainstem signaling and central respiratory control are defining mechanisms of this central sleep apnea syndrome; structural brain injury is not required for primary.
